basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 12-15.' and it opens 'VERS. 12-15.-- Respondit Abraham: Alias autem vere soror mea est, filia patris mei, et'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 12-15.-- Respondit Abraham: Alias autem vere soror mea est, filia patris mei, et non filia matris meae. Pater enim, ut nonnulli volunt, pro fratre ponitur, Thara itaque genuit Abraham, et Aran, cujus | filia exstitit, Scriptura teste, Saraa. Et ideo dixit, sororem suam esse, sive quia de semine su patris procreando per filium nata est Saraa, et consuetudo est etiam Scripturarum consobrinos fratres appellari, similiter et sorores. Propterea non immerito ait: Alias soror mea est. Et quia fuerunt Abraham et Aran de uno patre, et non de una matre, idcirco subjunxit, filia patris mei, et non filia matris meae.
